faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about WebP to AVIF conversion

items.question: Why convert WebP to AVIF if WebP is already good?
items.answer: AVIF provides 20-30% better compression than WebP with same or better quality. While WebP is excellent, AVIF is the next evolution with AV1 codec technology, HDR support, and 10-bit/12-bit color depth. For performance-critical sites and premium content, AVIF's additional compression and quality benefits are significant. AVIF is the future of web images with 92%+ browser support.

items.question: How much smaller are AVIF files compared to WebP?
items.answer: AVIF provides 20-30% better compression than WebP at equivalent quality. For example, a 500KB WebP might become 350-400KB as AVIF with same or better visual quality. This is in addition to WebP's 25-35% improvement over JPG, making AVIF 50-70% smaller than original JPG. Actual savings depend on image content - photos with complex textures see excellent compression.

items.question: Which browsers support AVIF format?
items.answer: AVIF has 92%+ browser support as of 2024. Supported by Chrome 85+ (2020), Firefox 93+ (2021), Safari 16+ (2022), Edge 121+ (2024), and Opera 71+ (2020). Mobile support includes Chrome Android, Safari iOS 16+, and Samsung Internet 14+. Implement triple fallback: AVIF → WebP → JPG for universal compatibility. WebP already has 95%+ support, so adding AVIF targets the most modern browsers.

items.question: Will converting WebP to AVIF affect image quality?
items.answer: Quality depends on original WebP: 1) Lossless WebP → AVIF: Quality preserved, 20-30% smaller. 2) Lossy WebP → AVIF: Current quality preserved but cannot restore lost data. AVIF can match WebP quality at 20-30% smaller size or provide better quality at same size. Use AVIF quality 50-55 to match WebP quality 80-85. Compare visually before deploying.

items.question: Should I upgrade all WebP images to AVIF?
items.answer: For modern, performance-critical websites, yes - AVIF's additional 20-30% compression is valuable. However: 1) Implement triple fallback (AVIF → WebP → JPG), 2) Monitor browser support (92%+ for AVIF vs 95%+ for WebP), 3) Consider encoding time (AVIF is slower), 4) Use quality 50-55 for optimal balance. AVIF is ideal for sites prioritizing cutting-edge performance with modern browser support.

items.question: Is WebP to AVIF conversion free and secure?
items.answer: Yes, our WebP to AVIF converter is completely free with no registration, watermarks, or payment required. All conversion happens locally in your browser using WebAssembly - your images never leave your device. This ensures 100% privacy and security, with no server uploads, data collection, or third-party access. WebP decoding and AVIF encoding are performed entirely client-side.
